description.text: Our mission is to provide clean energy to feed and fuel the world sustainably. With our employees focused on safe and reliable operations, environmental stewardship, and disciplined capital and corporate management, we are on a path to decarbonize our ammonia production network – the world’s largest – to enable low-carbon hydrogen and nitrogen products for energy, fertilizer, emissions abatement and other industrial activities. Our value chain consists of manufacturing complexes in the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom, an extensive storage, transportation and distribution network in North America, and logistics capabilities enabling a global reach. In July 2025, we completed a significant decarbonization project at our Donaldsonville, Louisiana, complex to enable the production of low-carbon ammonia. Additionally, we are executing further decarbonization projects in our existing network and constructing a greenfield low-carbon ammonia plant at our Blue Point complex to drive our strategy to leverage our unique capabilities to accelerate the world’s transition to clean energy. Our principal customers are cooperatives, retailers, independent fertilizer distributors, traders, wholesalers and industrial users. Our core product is anhydrous ammonia (ammonia), which contains 82% nitrogen and 18% hydrogen. Products derived from ammonia that are most often used as nitrogen fertilizers include granular urea, urea ammonium nitrate solution (UAN) and ammonium nitrate (AN).

analysis_md:
# CF — CF Industries Holdings, Inc.
Engine 5.4.0 run, 2026-10-16. In scope: market cap $19.602B (key_numbers.md) at $120.85 (nasdaq_quote_api).

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, fundamentals.json or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Pure-play North American nitrogen fertilizer producer: ammonia, granular urea, UAN, ammonium nitrate and diesel exhaust fluid, sold primarily into the U.S. Corn Belt from Gulf Coast and inland plants. The business is an energy-spread trade — natural gas is the feedstock and most of the cash cost, nitrogen products are global commodities — with a low-carbon angle in construction: the Blue Point blue-ammonia joint venture in Louisiana (CF 40%, partners JERA and Mitsui) started construction in 2026, targets 2029 operations, and CF's share of the spend is roughly $2B (via search of Q2 2026 reporting).

Current state (via search): tight global nitrogen supply-demand through 2026 into 2027 on management's outlook; H1 2026 net earnings rose 92.3% YoY and adjusted EBITDA rose 54.8% on higher average selling prices; Q2 2026 revenue was $2.22B (+17.6% YoY) but sales volume fell 15.3% YoY, in part because the Yazoo City complex has been idled since a November 2025 incident, with restart now expected in H1 2027, not late 2026. Gross ammonia production in 2026 is guided to ~9.5M tons including that outage. The quarterly dividend was raised 20% to $0.60 in July 2026, and ~2M shares were repurchased for $225M in Q2 2026.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $2,752,000,000; capex $950,000,000; SBC $45,000,000 (always a real cost, and trivial here).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $1,757,000,000 = $10.83/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $10.83)
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC, financials_history.csv): $1,770,000,000 — essentially the same as the conservative figure, which raises confidence in the FY2025 cash earnings.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years (key_numbers.md). Net debt $1.233B (key_numbers.md), 0.63x normalized OE (diagnostics).
- History is the warning label: OE/share was $10.77 (FY2021), $16.46 (FY2022 spike), $11.46 (FY2023), $9.50 (FY2024), $10.83 (FY2025) in financials_history.csv, and $4.17 in FY2020 — this is a cyclical spread business, not a compounder.

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math):**
- OCF: FY $2,752,000,000 − prior YTD $1,149,000,000 + current YTD $1,374,000,000 = **TTM $2,977,000,000**
- Capex: FY $950,000,000 − prior YTD $377,000,000 + current YTD $494,000,000 = **TTM $1,067,000,000**
- SBC: FY $45,000,000 − prior YTD $22,000,000 + current YTD $20,000,000 = **TTM $43,000,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **154,200,000**
- **TTM OE total $1,867,000,000 → base OE/share $12.11** (base_source: ttm_json)
- The engine's normalized base (3-yr median) is $10.83/share. The TTM base is used because the fiscal year ended 9.5 months ago (STALE_FY) and the TTM legs are clean filing math with no working-capital distortion flagged — but it is a favorable-cycle base: TTM revenue in fundamentals.json is $7,739,000,000 (+20.0% YoY) at a 42.5% gross margin, above every full year except the FY2022 spike. That cyclicality is handled in the scenario weights (45% on bear-or-worse), not by pretending the TTM did not happen. On the median base the preliminary default run gave a weighted IRR of 14.31% and IV@15% of $113.78 — Tier C as well, so the base choice does not drive the tier.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow; a cost moat, not a franchise
Justification: Structural low-cost position from North American Henry Hub / AECO natural gas (70-90% of nitrogen production cost) versus European/Asian rivals on imported LNG, plus scale, 98% ammonia capacity utilization in H1 2026 vs an ~86% North American peer benchmark, and a Mississippi River / pipeline logistics network into the Corn Belt — against pure commodity price-taker economics: undifferentiated nitrogen products, no pricing power, earnings set by the global nitrogen price and the gas spread.
- FOR: Low-cost North American natural gas feedstock (Henry Hub/AECO) vs European/Asian rivals on high-cost imported LNG — gas is 70-90% of nitrogen cash cost; scale and operating excellence (~98% of available ammonia capacity utilized in H1 2026 vs ~86% North American peer benchmark); Mississippi River, pipeline and rail logistics network from Gulf Coast plants (Donaldsonville) into the U.S. Corn Belt; ROIC proxy above 20% in each of FY2023-FY2025 and positive through the FY2020 trough (9.4%); disciplined capital return — diluted shares fell from 216.2M (FY2021) to 162.2M (FY2025) to 154.2M current-YTD (ttm.py), dividend raised 20% to $0.60/qtr in July 2026.
- AGAINST: Commodity price-taker — ammonia, urea, UAN and AN are undifferentiated and priced globally; earnings hostage to the nitrogen price / gas spread (revenue went $11.186B in FY2022 to $5.936B in FY2024 in two years, financials_history.csv); the cost advantage narrows if U.S. gas rises or overseas gas falls, and new capacity — including CF's own Blue Point (2029) — adds supply; concentration/outage risk (Yazoo City, up to 1.3M tons, idled since Nov 2025, restart pushed to H1 2027; Q2 2026 sales volume −15.3% YoY, via search); capex intensity rising (TTM capex $1.067B vs $0.453B-$0.518B/yr in FY2022-FY2024, ttm.json / financials_history.csv).
- ROIC / margin evidence (fundamentals.json, roic_proxy and gross margin): FY2020 ROIC 9.4% at a 19.4% gross margin; FY2021 28.0% / 36.5%; FY2022 73.3% / 52.4%; FY2023 27.4% / 38.4%; FY2024 23.1% / 34.6%; FY2025 30.4% / 38.5%; TTM gross margin 42.5%. Returns well above the cost of capital in the last five years are real, but they are spread-driven — the FY2022 spike and the FY2020 trough are the same business at different gas/fertilizer prices — so a moat above 6 would need pricing power or switching costs CF does not have.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — 5.4 final run (2026-10-16)
The engine's blended growth start is 6.83% (components, key_numbers.md: rev CAGR 5y 11.43%, rev CAGR 3y −14.12%, latest rev YoY 19.34%, OE/share CAGR 2y −2.78%, share count CAGR −7.39% with a 5.00% growth adjustment applied to the revenue components only). The 3-yr CAGR is a base-effect artifact of the FY2022 price spike (see BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT) and the 5-yr CAGR straddles it; neither was recalibrated away, because the blend's median lands near what the cleaner signals say — TTM OE/share growth in fundamentals.json is modest against FY2025 ($12.11 TTM base vs $10.83 latest FY) and per-share growth is carried substantially by the shrinking share count, which is actually happening (buybacks of $958,000,000 TTM in fundamentals.json). Scenario starts use the default offsets (−12/−5/0/+5/+12pp) and default OE multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Probabilities are skewed bearish vs the 10/25/30/25/10 defaults to 15/30/30/15/10: CF is being valued at a favorable point in its cycle (tight supply, price-driven prints, stock +54.86% YTD in prices.json), and its own history says OE/share can halve in two years.

Sanity check vs actual prints: scenario starts are OE/share growth, not revenue growth. Recent revenue prints are price-spike prints — latest FY rev YoY +19.34%, TTM revenue +20.0% YoY (fundamentals.json), Q2 2026 revenue +17.6% YoY on volume down 15.3% (via search) — while cash OE grew far less (TTM OE total $1,867,000,000 vs FY2025 $1,757,000,000, ttm.json / key_numbers.md) because capex stepped up to $1.067B TTM. So the base start (6.8%) sits below the revenue prints for a stated reason: the prints are nitrogen-price, not volume or cash-earnings, growth, and prices mean-revert. The bull (11.8%) and super-bull (18.8%) starts are the cases where tight supply into 2027 keeps the spread wide and buybacks keep compounding per-share OE; the super-bear start (−5.2% with a 0.75x OE multiplier) is still gentler than the actual FY2022→FY2024 OE/share path ($16.46 → $9.50), which is why the bear-side probabilities carry 45%.
